title: Space Invaders
lede: Tomohiro Nishikado’s arcade game for Taito made rows of two-frame bitmap aliens the first icons of video game pixel art.
summary: Rows of two-frame bitmap aliens over bunkers and a laser cannon, in black and white with colored cellophane strips. Taito, 1978.

creator.name: Tomohiro Nishikado for Taito; distributed outside Japan by Midway

evidence.note: Based on the Wikipedia article and its cited sources. No image was inspected for this record: the game graphics are in copyright, and no open, verified image was found.

styles.note: A founding work of the style: hand-drawn bitmap sprites with two-frame animation, which the style record names as the start of its era.

context: Wikipedia calls Space Invaders a 1978 fixed shooter developed and published by Taito for arcades, released in Japan in July 1978 and abroad through Midway later that year. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Invaders).

Nishikado created bitmap images of octopus-like aliens after *The War of the Worlds*, with other aliens after squids and crabs. After he drew the pixel art, he made a tool to animate two frames of movement for each character and adjusted the designs on screen with a light pen. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Invaders).

The game runs on an Intel 8080 and draws raster graphics through a bitmapped framebuffer. The hardware could not show color, so the first releases have black-and-white graphics with strips of orange and green cellophane over parts of the screen. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Invaders).
Wikipedia says the pixelated aliens “have become pop culture icons, sometimes representing video games as a whole”. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Space_Invaders).
interpretation: The two-frame aliens are the model for the style’s motion rule: animation steps between a few frames, with no easing.
The cellophane strips show that the first color in the style came from hardware limits, as bands of flat color, not shading.
borrow: Animate small sprites with two frames that alternate in step with movement.
Color whole horizontal bands of a monochrome screen instead of shading single objects.
next: Find an openly licensed image of the original arcade screen or of the alien bitmaps, and check its rights.

rights.statement: Commercial game graphics by Taito, in copyright. Link and metadata only.
